last_attempts_log.asr_text: What's more, when you draw a card rated UR or higher, the bonus jackpot begins, and you can keep opening packs. You're happy about one rare card, and then you get more time to open packs. Your willpower is just about to stand up and say, "All right, time to review!" when just one more tugs at its sleeve. What might happen here is not that you lose interest in English words, it's that the reason for your interest changes. You go from "I draw a card because I want to learn" to "I look at words because I want to draw a card." Even if you're looking at the same cards, the person in charge inside your mind has changed from the study worker to the treasure hunter. But here's something worth underlining in red: just because a word is rare doesn't mean it should be high on your study list. Rarity is simply the game's way of sorting words by how often they are used. "I'm happy I drew it and I should learn it first" are two separate things. Even if it shines, it doesn't get special treatment in your study order.
